items.author: Ben (2026-09-17, cutting the Digitisation build plan: elicitation form); Claude (item text, from a seven-lane read of the engine with an adversarial cross-check)
items.title: What 300 more years cost: exploration_sweep runs the shipped world through 1960 and times each span half per seed
items.design:
WHY. DIGITISATION.md § Open questions asks whether 300 years on the shared engine is affordable at Exploration's region counts, and no measured figure exists: the only Release numbers are ~6.2 s/seed to 1660 (2026-09-14, before BL-1007) and 38.6 s/seed for a full world plus an Empires re-run. The cost lane's estimate of 1-4 s/seed for 1660 -> 1960 is inference.

WHAT "THROUGH 1960" MEANS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. `world_params::exploration_stop_year = 1960` with `epoch_year` left at 0: the shipped world, with Exploration's own call running on to 1960 (190 rounds at its 4-year band). NEVER `epoch_year = 1960`, which selects the superseded 1160 -> 1560 -> 1960 two-span arc with Exploration off (era_minus_one.cpp:25-35, 365-370; DIGITISATION.md, opening: a 1960 epoch names a calendar). The extended span runs Exploration's forces only, with the Empires-round overrides off (era_minus_one.cpp:372-405); the face says so on every run.

THE WORK. exploration_sweep gains `--through <year>` (default 1660): generation and the traced acceptance re-run both stop there, so the existing acceptance check still holds the re-run to generation. A cost pass per seed times UNTRACED re-runs from the fixture to 1660 and to --through, and prints wall ms for each, the history_sim_last_profile split (demography, decisions, battles, reach), decision rounds, reach rebuilds, and regions and living polities at 1200, 1660 and 1960. The 1660 -> 1960 cost is the difference, labelled as such. A saturation line per half — battles and conquests per century, exploration tree nodes held — says whether the stretched world is still moving, so a frozen 1960 world reads as an inherited finding, not a Digitisation result.

DONE WHEN. A per-seed table over the sixteen library seeds, written to --out; the acceptance check green at --through 1960 on every seed; a stated wall-clock budget per seed for the span, quoted with the build tree.

RUN CONDITIONS (sprint 43, all items): one lane, serial, in the main session; Release harness builds via `bash tools/verify/build_lua_harness.sh <name>` into build_gen/verify, never %TEMP%; timings on a quiet machine with the build tree quoted; never write over a tracked sweep artefact (use --out). No item in this sprint changes a shipped world.

items.title: Both inherited weaknesses counted per seed at 1660 and 1960 — contact, binding, alarm saturation and displacement — for Ben's ruling at the sprint 43 gate
items.design:
WHY. NEXT_SESSION (2026-09-17) names two weaknesses Digitisation inherits: displacement held only against a saturated alarm (pooled 2.73 -> 0.50 when alarm tracked measured capability, no weight restoring it above 0.81), and polities rarely meet (stay-home verbs win 78.6% where an unmet target clears). RULED (Ben, 2026-09-17, elicitation): measure both in sprint 43 and rule at the gate. The evidence is weaker than the statement: the 78.6% and the corrected first-contact count (3..221 per seed) sit on unmerged commits eaf15a37 and 6d7bb462 on a world that is not main; main's sweep shows 412 first-crossing campaigns chosen over 16 seeds and 0 of 265 in-span pairs treaty-bound.

THE WORK. On the --through runs of BL-1027, report per seed for the 1200 -> 1660 half and the 1660 -> 1960 half: first contacts, split into battle crossings and inherited; pairs first met after 1200 that hold any treaty (met_pairs_bound); the share of alarm reads at the ceiling, beside near_alarm_max_q; pooled and median displacement; the contact-class campaign funnel (near / met in span / unmet: examined, in reach, cleared, chosen); trade-flow volume crossing landmasses. The existing counters are in exploration_sweep.cpp (near_alarm_max_q, met_pairs_bound, cross_landmass_volume, the displacement block). Port ONLY the trace-only halves of eaf15a37 (first contacts by kind, the unmet contest) and 6d7bb462 (the alarm spread) — never 6d7bb462's re-scaled visible_capability_reference, which moves the world.

DETERMINISM. A counter the harness cannot read off state or trace sits on history_sim_state as a pure, decision-free counter in the BL-926 idiom. Proof is world_determinism and the goldens holding bit-identical, stated in the close; any moved digest means a counter touched a decision and the item is not done.

DONE WHEN. The per-seed table at both halves, written to --out; digests unmoved; a NEEDS_REVIEW decision entry at the sprint 43 gate puts W1 (inherit, or revisit the capability reference) and W2 (inherit and produce contact in Digitisation, or a first-crossing force in Exploration) to Ben with these readings, read per seed, never the median.

RUN CONDITIONS (sprint 43, all items): one lane, serial, in the main session; Release harness builds via `bash tools/verify/build_lua_harness.sh <name>` into build_gen/verify, never %TEMP%; timings on a quiet machine with the build tree quoted; never write over a tracked sweep artefact (use --out). No item in this sprint changes a shipped world.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-17, cutting the Digitisation build plan: elicitation form); Claude (item text, from a seven-lane read of the engine with an adversarial cross-check)
items.title: digitisation_sim_harness reads the shipped world continued to 1960 beside a 1660 control, and says on its face what each of the thirteen readings is
items.design:
WHY. BL-982 (Digitisation readings) generates at epoch 0 and reads the 1660 close: 3 measured, 1 partial, 9 n/a (NR-886 item 7). Its recorded baseline (6/16, 0, 12/16, 0.48/0.74/0.82) and built exe predate wave A. The measure-before-mechanism slice gives every reading a real 1960 baseline before any Digitisation mechanism is admitted.

WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT MOVE, said on the face. Real 1960 values: reading 5's present half (mixed cities) and reading 7 (far trade, as standing flows). Newly measurable from existing state: reading 10 (subjects at 1660 and 1960, plus subject_freed events after 1660 split by whether a war freed them) and reading 9's urban half (urban share of population at 1660 and 1960). Inputs moved only: reading 1 and reading 6's proxy. STRUCTURAL ZEROS, printed as such and never counted measured: reading 3 (the recipe band follows epoch_year, ancient at epoch 0) and reading 8's region half (Stage 4 lag is computed only for a settlement stop >= 1700). Polity industrial crossings still move and are printed. n/a until their mechanism: 2, 4, 11, 12, 13, 5's concentration half, 9's cross-border half. The far-trade reading of BL-1006 (haulage_measure) runs epoch_year 1960, the superseded arc; the face records that it moves with the epoch flip, not here.

THE WORK. `--through <year>` sets exploration_stop_year (default 1660; this sprint runs 1960), epoch_year stays 0. Per seed: the world through --through, as today up to the applied search winner; a 1660 control re-run from the captured fixture (exploration_sweep.cpp:566-590, reading fx.works); the control's fingerprint counters must equal the library fingerprint from BL-1026, which proves the extended run agrees with the shipped world at 1660. Every face line names its surface and its year. SUMMARY counts measured, partial, structural zero and n/a separately (today it counts reading 3 as measured). Handoff violations from generation_report are printed per seed, and a seed with one reports no reading as measured. Output also to a per-seed JSON via --out.

DONE WHEN. The sixteen library seeds read at 1660 and 1960, per seed; every control matches its fingerprint; no src/world change; the SUMMARY and every structural zero honest. NR-886 item 7 is answered by the run and noted there.

RUN CONDITIONS (sprint 43, all items): one lane, serial, in the main session; Release harness builds via `bash tools/verify/build_lua_harness.sh <name>` into build_gen/verify, never %TEMP%; timings on a quiet machine with the build tree quoted; never write over a tracked sweep artefact (use --out). No item in this sprint changes a shipped world.
